nodes.description: Public state variable holding the Registry interface instance used for attribute lookups and writes.
Constant bytes32 attribute key 'isDepositAddress' used when registering deposit addresses.
Constructor that casts the supplied address into the Registry interface and stores it in registry.
Public function deriving a shifted address from msg.sender, checking the registry attribute and storing msg.sender as attribute value.
Payable fallback function that registers the deposit address and refunds msg.value to the caller.
msg.sender, an attacker-controlled address used for shifting, registration and the refund transfer.
External call to registry.setAttributeValue, interacting with a potentially untrusted registry contract.
External view call to registry.hasAttribute used in the require guard.
External value transfer msg.sender.transfer(msg.value) that sends Ether to an untrusted caller.
Constructor parameter _registry holding the address later cast to the Registry interface.
Local variable shiftedAddress = address(uint(msg.sender) >> 20) computed from msg.sender.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns the cast Registry instance into the registry state variable.
Constructor parameter _registry flows into the constructor body.
shiftedAddress is derived from msg.sender via a right shift.
msg.sender (as uint) is written into the registry attribute, binding the account to the shifted address.
Ether is sent back to the untrusted msg.sender, enabling reentrant behavior.
registerDepositAddress calls registry.hasAttribute inside the require guard.
registerDepositAddress performs the external registry.setAttributeValue call.
The fallback function executes the msg.sender.transfer refund.
Transferring Ether to msg.sender can re-enter the payable fallback before state changes settle.

normalization_plan.reason: The constructor parameter _registry is only used to initialize the registry state variable inside the constructor.
shiftedAddress is a temporary local computed and consumed solely inside registerDepositAddress.
